Generally, though, lavender fields across the country burst into vibrant hues from mid-July through August. During this time, the lavender reaches its peak bloom, painting landscapes with stunning shades of purple and captivating visitors with its delightful fragrance.

Moving southward, the lavender season in central regions such as the picturesque Kawaguchiko area near Mount Fuji usually begins in early July and continues through August. Dementia Care Through Aroma #3: Lavender
Lavender is not a panacea

When people think of aroma, many likely think of lavender (scientific name Lavandula angustifolia). It has a well-established image of calmness and restful sleep, and is treated as synonymous with essential oils.
However, in studies conducted on elderly people with dementia, its effects were not necessarily as expected.
This time, I will discuss a randomized controlled trial conducted by O’Connor et al. in 2013.

Unusually for aroma research, it employed a single-blind design where observers were unaware of the intervention, and a crossover design with alternating periods of using and not using aroma, which is a relatively high-evidence-level design.

In this study, lavender essential oil was applied to the arms of elderly people with severe dementia living in nursing facilities, and changes in BPSD (behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia) such as agitation and restlessness were observed.
